item.title: Trump says U.S. and Canada reached deal to delay 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports
item.description: President Trump said he was delaying the 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal less than two hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.

item.title: An iconic mail-order music and video company is shutting down
item.description: The long-running mail-order business Columbia House, which became famous for its record and CD clubs before focusing on DVDs, has announced it'll take its final orders next month.
item.content:encoded: The long-running mail-order business Columbia House, which became famous for its record and CD clubs before focusing on DVDs, has announced it'll take its final orders next month.

item.title: Flexibility is a key part of keeping women employed
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with University of Michigan economist Betsey Stevenson about trends in women's participation in the labor force and the value of flexible work arrangements.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Juana Summers talks with University of Michigan economist Betsey Stevenson about trends in women's participation in the labor force and the value of flexible work arrangements.

item.title: ABC and Disney sue FCC, alleging First Amendment violations
item.description: The ABC network has sued the Federal Communications Commission, alleging that the Trump administration is violating its First Amendment rights by challenging ABC broadcast licenses and investigating the network's talk show The View.

item.title: 'Profits won.' The child safety trial against Meta kicks off in federal court
item.description: Opening arguments are underway in a trial that pits four states against the company that owns Facebook and Instagram. They allege that Meta knew its products could hook kids — and lied about the danger.

item.title: The grueling fight over who profits from AI music
item.description: AI can generate songs in seconds. But behind every AI track is a complicated question: Who should get paid? And, how? The fights have started.

item.title: Many recent grads say AI is making it harder to get a job. Economists aren't so sure
item.description: The unemployment rate for young adults with new degrees is higher than the rate for all workers, according to the New York Fed. Is AI the problem, or is it more complicated?

item.title: Cities are adopting new data center standards as public opposition grows
item.description: As the number of data centers across the U.S. continues to increase, so does public opposition. That has some cities changing their standards for what acceptable data center development looks like.

item.title: Meta heads to court in a landmark trial about kids and social media addiction
item.description: Four states are suing the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, alleging that the platforms were designed to hook kids and that Meta hid the mental health risks.

item.title: Living with nuns: Priced out of D.C., young women found low rent with unlikely roommates
item.description: For 10 years, a Catholic-run home offered young women an affordable place to live in the nation's capital as they studied and launched careers. Now, that community is saying goodbye.
